title: WATCH: Marcos calls for mutual respect at ASEAN-China meeting
summary: He called for mutual respect and practical cooperation at an ASEAN meeting.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged Southeast Asian leaders and China to exercise "self-restraint, mutual respect, and practical cooperation" as Manila's longstanding tensions with Beijing hang over broader efforts to deepen regional ties.
"Let us build on the achievements of our partners to advance peace, stability and prosperity in our region," Marcos said Monday, November 16, as he opened a meeting between ASEAN leaders and China.

Despite strains in Philippine-China relations, Marcos highlighted two milestones this year: the 35th anniversary of ASEAN-China dialogue relations and the fifth anniversary of their comprehensive strategic partnership.
"Since China was accorded dialogue partner status in 1996, our partnership has grown, delivering meaningful progress across all three pillars of cooperation," Marcos said.
He urged ASEAN and China to find common ground and pursue "tangible cooperation" amid regional and global uncertainty.
As one example, Marcos cited the adoption of a joint statement addressing the regional effects of developments in the Middle East.
